intro: Malibu is 21 miles of coastline along PCH, from Surfrider Beach and the pier to Zuma, Point Dume and the sea caves at El Matador. The restaurants lean on the views and the seafood, and the Santa Monica Mountains rise right behind the beach.

laist: LAist: Fire-affected restaurants open and closed in Malibu and the Palisades
gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites Nathaniel checked)

places.w: A well-run espresso bar with a garden patio out back.
places.o: A latte and an almond croissant in the garden.

places.w: A busy French-style cafe near Point Dume, popular after a morning hike.
places.o: A vanilla cold foam latte and the lobster burrito.

places.w: Oversized breakfast burritos and long lines.
places.o: Call your order in ahead.

places.w: A walk-up PCH stand where surfers grab breakfast burritos.
places.o: The breakfast burrito with bacon.

places.w: A breezy all-day restaurant at the end of the Malibu Pier.
places.o: Light salads or fish tacos with the view.

places.w: A casual Israeli patio across from Surfrider Beach.
places.o: The salmon kofta plate.

places.w: A tiny Spanish market making sandwiches on imported bread.
places.o: Go early; the daily sandwiches sell out.

places.w: A tiny roadside shack with fresh fish and chips.
places.o: Fish and chips and a shrimp cocktail on the patio.

places.w: Counter-service seafood with one of LA's best lobster rolls.
places.o: The hot buttered lobster roll.

places.w: A retro 1960s-style seafood stop at the far end of Malibu, famous with motorcyclists.
places.o: Clam chowder or anything fried.

places.w: An upscale raw bar with martinis.
places.o: Rockfish ceviche and a martini.

places.w: The glamorous oceanfront flagship.
places.o: Rock shrimp tempura and a sunset table.

places.w: A lively indoor-outdoor Greek restaurant in the Country Mart.
places.o: Grilled octopus and a whole branzino.

places.w: A classic white-tablecloth Italian spot since the early 1990s.
places.o: Jumbo gnocchi with veal ragu.

places.w: A steakhouse with a lively room and solid food.
places.o: Start with the shrimp cocktail.

places.w: A surf-themed oceanfront restaurant with strong margaritas, reopening in stages after fire damage.
places.o: A mai tai at the window. Check hours before you go.

places.w: The only Malibu restaurant actually on the sand. You come for the setting.
places.o: A cocktail with your feet in the sand.

places.a: Kanan Dume Rd and W Newton Canyon Rd
places.w: A local winery's tasting patio, reopened at a new canyon location after the fire.
places.o: Weekend afternoons only.

places.w: Malibu's historic pier next to the famous point break.
places.o: Watch the surfers from the pier in the morning.

places.w: A huge, clean stretch of sand with lifeguards, showers and easy parking right next to the water.
places.o: A full beach day with kids.

places.w: A beach and a short bluff hike with sweeping views, wildflowers in spring and whales in season.
places.o: Hike the headland at sunset.

places.w: A dramatic cove of sea stacks, arches and small caves at the bottom of a steep path.
places.o: Go for sunset, but leave before the lot closes.

places.w: The Getty's re-created Roman villa, with Greek and Roman antiquities and gardens above the ocean. Free with a timed reservation.
places.o: Reserve online and pay for parking; pair it with lunch on PCH. It stays open while the Getty Center closes for renovation in 2027, with some Center paintings on view here.

places.w: Canyon trails, a rock pool for swimming and the old M*A*S*H filming site.
places.o: Hike to the M*A*S*H site, about 2.5 miles each way.
